articles.title: Motociclista de 33 anos morre após ser atingido por carro na BR-364 | G1
articles.standfirst: Alan Santos seguia de moto pela rodovia quando foi atingido por um carro. Motorista do veículo deixou local antes da chegada das equipes de resgate.
articles.summary: Alan Santos seguia de moto pela rodovia quando foi atingido por um carro. Motorista do veículo deixou local antes da chegada das equipes de resgate.
articles.body:
Um motociclista identificado como Alan Santos, de 33 anos , morreu após um acidente envolvendo a moto que conduzia e um carro na BR-364, em Rondonópolis , a 218 km de Cuiabá, neste domingo (22). Alan morava e trabalhava em uma fazenda da região.

Segundo a Nova Rota do Oeste, concessionária que administra a rodovia, o acidente ocorreu no km 205. O carro teria tentado ultrapassar uma carreta quando atingiu a traseira da moto em que Alan estava. Com o impacto, o motociclista foi arremessado ao asfalto.

A concessionária informou que os socorristas foram até o local logo após o acidente e constataram que o motociclista já estava morto.

O motorista do carro e o veículo não foram encontrados quando as equipes chegaram. As circunstâncias do acidente devem ser investigadas.

A morte de Alan Santos foi constatada ainda no local — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Pescadores desaparecidos no Pantanal: Marinha faz buscas em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Janair Prudêncio e Israel Alves de Figueiredo sumiram após saírem de barco na região do Caronal, em Corumbá. Equipe da Marinha foi enviada para procurar os dois pescadores.
articles.summary: Marinha faz buscas por Janair Prudêncio e Israel Alves, pescadores desaparecidos no Pantanal após saírem de barco na região do Caronal, entre Corumbá e Coxim.
articles.body:
Rio Taquari, região de Coxim (MS) — Foto: Reprodução

Dois pescadores desapareceram na região do Caronal, no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul, entre Corumbá e Coxim. Eles foram identificados como Janair Prudêncio, conhecido como Gê, e Israel Alves de Figueiredo, chamado de Figueiredo.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, os dois foram vistos pela última vez na quarta-feira (18), quando estavam em uma área de pesca no Pantanal. Desde então, familiares e conhecidos não conseguiram mais contato com eles.

De acordo com o relato da filha de Janair à polícia, os dois almoçaram no barraco de um homem conhecido como Ramon Traíra. O local fica a cerca de 20 minutos de barco de um hotel flutuante.

Depois do almoço, Gê e Figueiredo seguiram rio abaixo, com destino ao barraco de Amaral, que fica a aproximadamente 60 quilômetros de distância.

A previsão era que eles chegassem ao destino ainda naquele dia. No entanto, por volta das 21h, como os pescadores não haviam aparecido, conhecidos começaram a desconfiar de que o barco poderia ter apresentado algum problema ou que algo mais grave tivesse acontecido.

Na manhã seguinte, Ramon e Amaral percorreram o trajeto que os pescadores deveriam ter feito, mas não encontraram a embarcação nem qualquer sinal dos dois homens.

A Marinha do Brasil informou que tomou conhecimento do desaparecimento dos dois homens e enviou uma equipe da Capitania Fluvial do Pantanal ao local para realizar buscas.

A corporação também informou que abriu um Inquérito Administrativo sobre Acidentes e Fatos da Navegação (IAFN) para apurar as circunstâncias do desaparecimento e verificar se houve algum fator relacionado à segurança da navegação.

A Marinha pede que qualquer informação que possa ajudar a localizar os pescadores seja comunicada pelo telefone 185, número de emergência marítima e fluvial.

Os filhos de Figueiredo também procuraram a polícia para registrar o desaparecimento do pai. Eles contaram que o pescador estava sem celular e havia combinado de entrar em contato com a família quando chegasse ao barraco de Ramon.

O combinado foi cumprido na quarta-feira (18), às 11h45, quando Figueiredo ligou para a mãe dos filhos usando o celular de Ramon.

Os familiares também informaram que havia a suspeita de que os pescadores estivessem com dois equipamentos de internet via satélite Starlink na embarcação. No entanto, os filhos de Figueiredo disseram que não sabem se o equipamento estava funcionando, pois o pai não havia pago pelo serviço.

A companheira de Janair também esteve na delegacia e confirmou as informações sobre o desaparecimento.

Até a última atualização, não havia informações sobre o paradeiro dos dois pescadores.

articles.title: Sánchez tenta impedir vitória da direita na Espanha e cita Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: País europeu terá eleições parlamentares antecipadas no domingo (29), e as pesquisas de intenção de voto mostram premiê atrás de candidato conservador. Partido Popular (PP), de direita, poderia buscar coalizão com extrema direita em eventual vitória no pleito.
articles.summary: País europeu terá eleições parlamentares antecipadas no domingo (29), e as pesquisas de intenção de voto mostram premiê atrás de candidato conservador. Partido Popular (PP), de direita, poderia buscar coalizão com extrema direita em eventual vitória no pleito.
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez, apresenta o plano de cidadania e integração, no encerramento do prazo para candidaturas à amnistia migratória, em Madrid, Espanha — Foto: REUTERS/Violeta Santos Moura

O primeiro-ministro socialista Pedro Sánchez tenta desafiar, nas eleições do próximo domingo (29), as pesquisas que antecipam uma vitória dos conservadores, que poderiam governar com o apoio da extrema direita —algo que seria inédito desde o fim da ditadura na Espanha .

O resultado das eleições antecipadas, inicialmente previstas para 2027, será acompanhado de muito perto nas capitais europeias, já que pode alterar os equilíbrios dentro da União Europeia (UE). Além disso, o bloco terá uma série de votações decisivas em 2027, na França, Polônia e Itália.

"Rumo à vitória, vamos votar, vencer e governar por mais quatro anos", afirmou Sánchez durante um comício no fim de semana. Ele também voltou a citar a reeleição do presidente Lula e pediu para que os eleitores sigam o exemplo brasileiro por meio da mobilização popular (leia mais abaixo) .

O político socialista de 54 anos se consolidou como um líder internacional da esquerda durante seu governo, que já dura oito anos. No entanto, ele se tornou uma figura altamente polarizadora na Espanha e atualmente aparece nas pesquisas de intenção de voto atrás de Alberto Núñez Feijóo , líder do Partido Popular (PP, de direita), de 65 anos. Mas a diferença diminuiu nos últimos dias.

"Não confiem nas pesquisas (...) Nós os conhecemos, são capazes de tudo e, feridos, são ainda mais perigosos", advertiu Feijóo em um evento de campanha, no qual foi categórico: "A Espanha precisa de limpeza. A Espanha precisa de mudança e, juntos, vamos conseguir isso".

As pesquisas apontam uma vitória do PP, mas longe da maioria absoluta no Congresso , em uma repetição do resultado das legislativas de 2023, quando, apesar de ter ficado em segundo lugar, Sánchez conseguiu reunir apoios para ser reeleito.

Assim, o PP pode precisar do apoio do partido de extrema direita Vox, terceira força política do país , que quase dobraria o número de cadeiras no Congresso.

Vox e PP já governam juntos várias regiões, mas a extrema direita não participa do governo central desde o retorno da democracia, após a morte do ditador Francisco Franco, em 1975.

A situação de Sánchez é mais complicada devido à fragilidade de outros partidos de esquerda, cujo apoio foi crucial para mantê-lo no poder em 2023.

Em comício no final de semana, Pedro Sánchez pediu aos eleitores que evitem "o retrocesso" —que, segundo ele, significaria um eventual governo de coalizão entre PP e Vox—, após os avanços de seu governo na área social, para o feminismo e os direitos LGBTQIA+, tudo isso enquanto a economia espanhola, a quarta maior da UE, mantém seu dinamismo.

“Se tudo isso conseguimos com um governo de coalizão em minoria parlamentar, o que não poderíamos conseguir para Canárias e para a Espanha com um Governo de maioria absoluta de cadeiras e deputados e deputadas progressistas? Por isso é preciso se mobilizar, é preciso ir votar no próximo dia 29 de novembro e é preciso votar na cor vermelha do Partido Socialista. É isso que temos de fazer para frear a involução: mobilização. Essa é a única receita, a que tiveram nos Estados Unidos, a que Lula teve no Brasil e a que teremos na Espanha no próximo dia 29 de novembro”, afirmou Sánchez em um comício nas Canárias.

Presidente da Internacional Socialista, o premiê espanhol já entrou em choque com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e com o premiê israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu, por conta das guerras no Irã e em Gaza. Além disso, na contramão de muitos de seus parceiros europeus, Sánchez é um defensor da imigração em uma Espanha que envelhece e precisa de mão de obra.

Sánchez tentou capitalizar a indignação diante da crise de acesso à moradia na Espanha e conseguiu aprovar medidas para restringir despejos forçados e a aquisição de imóveis por grandes fundos de investimento.

Porém, qualquer benefício eleitoral para Sánchez parece incerto. A oposição o culpa por não conseguir frear o aumento dos custos da moradia e dos bens de consumo em geral.

Sánchez "tem que sair já, por decência e por respeito aos espanhóis. Feijóo não sei se é o candidato (ideal), mas precisamos de mudança", afirmou à agência de notícias AFP Pedro Suárez, um empresário de 64 anos.

"Eu acho que este país avançou bastante nos últimos anos. Muitas coisas foram conquistadas na área social", declarou Pilar Sánchez, de 64 anos, eleitora do chefe de Governo socialista.

Feijóo, que governou a Galícia durante 13 anos, pede a renúncia de Sánchez há vários anos devido aos escândalos de corrupção em seu entorno, pelas concessões aos independentistas da Catalunha e por sua incapacidade de aprovar o orçamento do Estado.

Com a promessa de uma "regeneração institucional", o PP também critica a avalanche de migrantes em julho na cidade espanhola de Ceuta, localizada no norte da África, e as duas colisões de trens de alta velocidade neste ano, que provocaram 115 mortes.

Por sua vez, o Vox destacou em sua campanha seu discurso anti-imigração.

"Aqui há muitas pessoas que estão vivendo de benefícios sociais que são necessários aos espanhóis e que não têm que estar na Espanha . Estas pessoas, nós vamos convidar que retornem", disse em um comício o líder do partido, Santiago Abascal, antes de afirmar que os "estupradores" e "assassinos" devem estar "nas prisões de seus países".

articles.title: Natal em Petrolina: Chegada do Papai Noel abre campanha da CDL | G1
articles.standfirst: Consumidores que adquirirem produtos nas lojas credenciadas vão participar de sorteios em dezembro. Ação também arrecadou donativos para a ONG Anjos da Esperança.
articles.summary: Natal em Petrolina inicia com a Corrida Mágica e doações; clientes das lojas credenciadas concorrem a um carro zero, iPhones e prêmios em dinheiro em dezembro.
articles.body:
Papai Noel da CDL e Sindilojas chega durante corrida em Petrolina — Foto: Divulgação/ CDL

A "Corrida Mágica" marcou a chegada do Papai Noel e abriu a campanha "Natal da Cidade" no domingo (22), em Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco. O evento foi promovido pela Câmara de Dirigentes Lojistas (CDL) e pelo Sindicato do Comércio Varejista (Sindilojas).

Os participantes da corrida escolheram entre percursos de 3 km e 5 km. Além da prática esportiva, a ação teve caráter solidário com arrecadação de brinquedos para a ONG Anjos da Esperança.

Durante a campanha natalina, os consumidores que comprarem nas lojas credenciadas vão concorrer a prêmios no dia 29 de dezembro. Serão sorteados um carro zero quilômetro, dois iPhones e valores em dinheiro (R$ 15 mil, R$ 10 mil e R$ 5 mil).

articles.title: Zelensky reivindica ataque contra navio de guerra russo na Líbia | G1
articles.standfirst: Navio de guerra Merkury foi destruído no domingo (23) após ser atingido por drones de ataque ucranianos em base naval de Benghazi, segundo Volodymyr Zelensky. Cargueiro MV Angara, acusado de transportar armamentos russos, também foi atacado na região.
articles.summary: Navio de guerra Merkury foi destruído no domingo (23) após ser atingido por drones de ataque ucranianos em base naval de Benghazi, segundo Volodymyr Zelensky. Cargueiro MV Angara, acusado de transportar armamentos russos, também foi atacado na região.
articles.body:
A Ucrânia afundou duas embarcações russas na costa da Líbia , incluindo um navio de guerra que estava atracada em uma base militar, em um ataque de drones chamado de "exemplar" pelo presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , nesta segunda-feira (23).

Os ataques ocorreram no domingo e sete drones marítimos foram utilizados ao todo, afirmou Zelensky.

A corveta Merkury , um navio de guerra russo de última geração , estava atracada na base naval Benghazi , no norte do país africano, quando foi atingida e afundou, segundo Zelensky.

O cargueiro russo MV Angara , que estava a seis quilômetros da costa da cidade líbia e era acusado por Zelensky de transportar armamentos, também foi atingido.

"Uma operação exemplar da Ucrânia em resposta à guerra da Rússia . (...) Nossos combatentes utilizaram sete drones navais de fabricação ucraniana e a corveta russa Merkury foi afundada, apesar de todos os esforços do inimigo para impedir o ataque. É uma das embarcações mais novas da Rússia, incorporada à frota em 2023, já durante a guerra. Nosso segundo alvo foi o navio russo de carga seca MV Angara, utilizado pelo inimigo para transportar armas", afirmou Zelensky em publicação nas redes sociais.

O presidente ucraniano divulgou um vídeo que mostra o momento dos ataques às duas embarcações. Nas imagens, é possível ver os drones marítimos se aproximando pela água e colidindo contra os navios russos , causando grandes explosões. Veja acima.

Zelensky acrescentou que um helicóptero de combate russo Ka-27 também foi destruído junto com a corveta Merkury. O Ministério da Defesa ucraniano afirma que não há rotas seguras para a armada russa, nem pra sua rede de logística.

Imagem de satélite mostra navio de guerra russo afundado na base naval Benghazi, na Líbia, após ataque de drones em 22 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Vantor/Handout via REUTERS

Além dos ataques na Líbia, a Ucrânia também bombardeou, no sábado, o cargueiro russo Sparta II no Golfo da Finlândia . "Continuamos nossas operações nas áreas marítimas designadas e estamos respondendo à agressão russa", disse Zelensky.

O governo do leste da Líbia afirmou que a Merkury estava atracada na base naval de Benghazi quando foi atingida pelos drones, e disse que o navio havia parado para reabastecer e receber suprimentos durante o trajeto de volta à Rússia, no âmbito de um acordo de cooperação.

O governo da Rússia, que está em guerra contra a Ucrânia há quase cinco anos, negou-se a comentar os ataques na Líbia e disse que seu Ministério da Defesa "está lidando com isso". Sobre o ataque contra o Sparta II, nesta segunda-feira o Kremlin acusou Kiev de terrorismo e disse que o incidente pode levar a uma escalada no mar Báltico.

A Líbia é um país mergulhado em um cenário de caos desde a queda do ditador Muammar Gaddafi, em 2011. Atualmente, permanece dividido entre um governo apoiado pela ONU, com sede em Trípoli, no oeste do país, e uma administração rival em Benghazi, no leste.

Bombardeio russo deixa mortos e feridos na região de Kiev

Bombeiros tentam apagar um incêndio após um ataque russo em Dymer, região de Kiev, Ucrânia, domingo, 22 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: AP/Efrem Lukatsky

Pelo menos 15 pessoas morreram em bombardeios russos que atingiram no domingo áreas próximas à capital ucraniana, onde equipes de resgate procuram moradores presos sob os escombros de um bloco de apartamentos que desabou parcialmente após o ataque.

A Rússia intensificou os ataques contra Kiev nos últimos seis meses, incluindo bombardeios contra áreas residenciais no momento em que o inverno (hemisfério norte) se aproxima, em meio à guerra, iniciada com a invasão de fevereiro de 2022.

Um ataque noturno contra Dymer, 45 quilômetros ao norte da capital ucraniana, atingiu um prédio de cinco andares e deixou pelo menos 11 mortos, segundo o governador da região de Kiev, Timur Tkachenko.

Quatro pessoas também morreram em outras regiões do estado de Kiev.

Vídeo mostra ataque de drones ucranianos a navio de guerra russo em base naval na Líbia em 22 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Volodymyr Zelensky

articles.title: Caos digital alimenta teorias de ataque cibernético nos Estados Unidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Cancelamento de voos, instabilidade em serviços e invasões hackers aumentam preocupações. Problema, no entanto, reflete cortes orçamentários da gestão Trump.
articles.summary: Cancelamento de voos, instabilidade em serviços e invasões hackers aumentam preocupações. Problema, no entanto, reflete cortes orçamentários da gestão Trump.
articles.body:
Cancelamento de voos, instabilidade em serviços e invasões hackers aumentam preocupações. Problema, no entanto, reflete cortes orçamentários da gestão Trump. — Foto: Kevin Horvart/Unplash

No último dia 12 de novembro, trabalhadores em todo o mundo tiveram uma surpresa desagradável. O software de e-mail Outlook havia paralisado. A plataforma de comunicação Teams estava extremamente lenta. A ferramenta de IA Copilot tinha ficado temporariamente indisponível.

Os três programas são da Microsoft , que levou cerca de 24 horas para restabelecer o funcionamento normal dos serviços . O prejuízo econômico global causado pela falha foi estimado em vários bilhões de dólares.

Segundo a empresa, o problema foi gerado por um erro de programação oculto no sistema desde julho, que acabou ativado por uma alteração no software e fez com que vários servidores deixassem de responder.

A instabilidade nos sistemas da Microsoft , no entanto, foi apenas o início de uma semana que quase não teve um dia sem uma nova falha cibernética grave.

Em 13 de novembro, o órgão federal de aviação dos Estados Unidos relatou um problema nos dispositivos que levou a uma pane aérea que afetou todos os aeroportos do país durante 4 horas.

Cerca de 12,5 mil voos tiveram que ser cancelados. Nos dias seguintes, houve outros incidentes. O ministro dos Transportes, Sean Duffy, explicou que um "volume excessivo de dados" havia sobrecarregado a obsoleta infraestrutura de hardware do serviço.

Ainda naquela noite, a empresa americana Workday relatou uma falha total do sistema, que se prolongou até o meio-dia do dia seguinte.

🔎 A Workday é uma das principais prestadoras de serviços de gestão de pessoal e folhas de pagamento. Aparentemente, um erro técnico de conexão teria paralisado dois centros de dados ao mesmo tempo.

Em 16 de novembro, a companhia aérea norte-americana United Airlines registrou uma "falha interna no sistema", que resultou em inúmeros atrasos nas decolagens.

No mesmo dia, um problema num software interno afetou várias transações online do banco JPMorgan Chase . No dia seguinte, foi a vez da gigante Apple .

Um erro na atualização interna de software da desenvolvedora teria sido o responsável por graves problemas em serviços como o iCloud, o Apple Pay e a App Store.

Nem mesmo os serviços de inteligência foram poupados. A Agência de Segurança Nacional (NSA) sofreu uma interrupção temporária na rede secreta de comunicação interna, a "NSA Net", supostamente causada por patches de software durante trabalhos de manutenção programados.

E, neste fim de semana, o FBI teria sofrido, segundo a imprensa americana, uma invasão hacker na plataforma de mandados judiciais , o segundo ataque cibernético sofrido pela agência de inteligência desde setembro.

Donald Trump fala durante coletiva à imprensa na Casa Branca. — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

Na semana passada, a Casa Branca se esforçou em dissipar as preocupações crescentes da população em relação a um ataque cibernético em grande escala.

"É assim que a vida é", declarou o presidente Donald Trump. "Quando você é grande, poderoso e tem tanto dinheiro, essas coisas simplesmente acontecem. Não há problema nisso", afirmou ele, durante viagem à Ásia.

Trump foi apoiado pelo secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio. "Não somos alvo de um ataque sistêmico. Esses incidentes não têm nada a ver uns com os outros, não há nenhuma conexão entre eles", afirmou Rubio.

Mas, na sexta-feira, Sean Cairncross, diretor nacional de segurança cibernética da Casa Branca, foi demitido. Antes disso, a gestão da crise do governo Trump havia sofrido críticas massivas.

Circulavam nas redes sociais, por exemplo, rumores sobre um apagão nacional iminente, o que levou a uma onda de compras nos EUA. Itens como geradores de energia, por exemplo, esgotaram-se das plataformas de e-commerce.

De fato, até o momento não há nenhuma evidência concreta de que os incidentes tenham sido provocados por ataques cibernéticos direcionados. No entanto, especulações são inevitáveis.

"Se tudo isso for apenas coincidência, então é a maior coincidência da história mundial", afirmou o senador republicano Josh Hawley. Ex-diretora da Agência Nacional de Segurança Cibernética (CISA), Jen Easterly acrescentou: "Nunca presenciei uma concentração de incidentes como essa durante meu mandato."

Especialistas em segurança cibernética atribuem a série de falhas, entre outros fatores, a atualizações defeituosas que se deparam com uma infraestrutura de TI parcialmente desatualizada .

Muitas empresas estariam detectando brechas de segurança cada vez mais rapidamente com o auxílio da inteligência artificial – e, em seguida, provocando involuntariamente novos erros no sistema por meio de atualizações precipitadas de software.

Por outro lado, crescem as críticas ao governo Trump. Desde o início de 2025, a gestão do republicano vem reduzindo drasticamente os recursos destinados à defesa cibernética.

Só a CISA já perdeu, nesse ínterim, cerca de um terço de seu quadro de funcionários. O Congresso – até o momento ainda dominado pelos republicanos – cortou o orçamento da agência em cerca de 300 milhões de dólares; para 2027, a Casa Branca propôs novos cortes de cerca de 700 milhões de dólares .

Dado o contexto, até mesmo republicanos de alto escalão estão se distanciando da linha oficial do governo.

Don Bacon, presidente da Comissão de Segurança Cibernética da Câmara dos Deputados, declarou recentemente em público que os cortes na segurança de TI foram excessivos.

"Precisamos de uma CISA forte para proteger as redes de energia elétrica e as redes nacionais", disse ele.

No X, o renomado historiador americano Timothy Snyder criticou, entre outras coisas, o fato de Trump ter extinguido agências de segurança cibernética em todo o aparato estatal. "Ele nos tornou vulneráveis", afirmou Snyder, "de uma forma que nenhum inimigo estrangeiro jamais conseguiria."

articles.title: Jensen Huang: Trump pede que Nvidia recontrate ex-CEO após polêmica | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido do presidente americano ocorre após jornal revelar que ex-amante do executivo manteve contato por mais de um ano com um agente da inteligência chinesa.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang recebe apoio de Trump para voltar à Nvidia após polêmica de espionagem chinesa e renúncia motivada por um suposto relacionamento extraconjugal.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, ao lado de Donald Trump, presidente dos Estados Unidos, em foto de 8 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Evan Vucci

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , pediu que o conselho de administração da Nvidia recontrate Jensen Huang, ex-presidente-executivo da companhia, que renunciou ao cargo em meio a um suposto escândalo de espionagem envolvendo uma mulher com quem manteve um relacionamento extraconjugal .

"Espero que o conselho da Nvidia recontrate Jensen Huang. Seria a melhor coisa para a empresa e também para os Estados Unidos", escreveu Trump nas redes sociais, na noite de domingo (22).

O apelo ocorreu após o jornal americano The New York Times revelar, também no domingo, que Alice Huang, apontada como ex-amante do executivo, manteve contato por mais de um ano com um funcionário da principal agência de espionagem da China .

Segundo a publicação, Alice manteve contato com um agente do Ministério da Segurança do Estado da China entre meados de 2025 e outubro deste ano, quando seu relacionamento com o então presidente-executivo da Nvidia veio a público.

A suposta amante de Huang comandou anteriormente a Megaspeed International, empresa sediada em Singapura que figura entre os principais clientes da Nvidia e chegou a movimentar bilhões em compras de chips da companhia.

Autoridades americanas investigam a Megaspeed desde 2024 por suspeitas de contrabando de chips avançados de inteligência artificial da Nvidia para a China.

As suspeitas desencadearam um escândalo que levou à renúncia de Jensen Huang duas semanas depois e provocou uma forte queda nas ações da Nvidia.

Integrantes do governo Trump afirmaram diversas vezes que ainda não há uma conclusão sobre o suposto envolvimento de Alice Huang em atividades de espionagem para a China.

O procurador-geral dos Estados Unidos, Todd Blanche, declarou neste mês que o Departamento de Justiça ainda não havia determinado se ela atuava como espiã chinesa.

Pressão pela volta de Jensen Huang à Nvidia

Nas últimas semanas, o jornal britânico Financial Times informou que Jensen Huang avalia a possibilidade de voltar ao comando da Nvidia .

Um aliado do executivo disse ao jornal que está sendo organizada uma "sala de guerra", com a participação de líderes do Vale do Silício, região dos Estados Unidos que concentra grandes empresas de tecnologia. O objetivo é pressionar pela volta do ex-CEO e conquistar o apoio da Casa Branca.

A campanha ganhou força no fim de semana, com o apoio de nomes como Elon Musk, presidente-executivo da Tesla e da SpaceX, e Tim Sweeney, fundador da Epic Games.

Eles estão entre os empresários que assinaram uma carta aberta pedindo ao conselho de administração da Nvidia que "traga Jensen de volta".

Funcionários da companhia também se manifestaram publicamente a favor do retorno de Huang e assinaram o documento.

A tentativa de reconduzir o executivo ao cargo, porém, enfrenta resistência em Washington. Neste domingo (22), o secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, defendeu uma "mudança drástica" na liderança da Nvidia após a saída de Huang.

Na última terça-feira (17), durante uma teleconferência com investidores após a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais da empresa, o presidente do conselho de administração da Nvidia, Harvey Jones, afirmou que a companhia não recontrataria seu cofundador para o cargo de CEO e que não responderia a perguntas sobre sua saída.

Jones também informou que o conselho contratou a consultoria de recrutamento Heidrick & Struggles para ajudar na escolha de um novo presidente-executivo.

"Queremos nomear um presidente-executivo permanente o mais rápido possível, mas não vamos apressar a decisão antes de encontrar a pessoa certa", afirmou.

articles.title: Feirão Negocia Manaus: descontos de até 100% em juros e multas | G1
articles.standfirst: Atendimento gratuito acontece até às 14h no shopping Phelippe Daou, no bairro Cidade de Deus. A ação reúne 16 empresas e instituições.
articles.summary: Com a participação de 16 empresas, o Feirão Negocia Manaus oferece perdão de juros e consultas de CPF no Shopping Phelippe Daou para regularização de dívidas.
articles.body:
Consumidores com contas em atraso podem negociar dívidas com descontos de até 100% em juros, multas e encargos durante a 4ª edição do Feirão Negocia Manaus , que começa nesta segunda-feira (23), na Zona Norte da capital. A ação reúne 16 empresas e instituições e oferece condições especiais de pagamento, incluindo opções de parcelamento.

O atendimento é gratuito e acontece até às 14h, no espaço de eventos da Secretaria Municipal do Trabalho, Empreendedorismo e Inovação (Semtepi), localizado no shopping Phelippe Daou, no bairro Cidade de Deus.

A iniciativa é realizada pela Prefeitura de Manaus, por meio do Procon Manaus. Os descontos e as condições de parcelamento variam de acordo com os critérios de cada empresa ou instituição participante.

Além de negociar dívidas diretamente com os credores, os consumidores que forem ao local poderão utilizar os seguintes serviços:

Emissão de boletos para regularização de dívidas cartoriais;

Consultoria voltada para pequenos negócios.

articles.title: Chuvas intensas no Sul do Rio e Costa Verde: Inmet emite alerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidades podem registrar 20 a 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia. Algumas cidades podem registrar números entre 30 a 60 mm/h ou 50 e 100 mm/dia com ventos intensos.
articles.summary: Chuvas intensas no Sul do Rio e Costa Verde podem chegar a 100 mm nesta segunda-feira, com riscos de alagamentos e quedas de árvores em 24 cidades da região.
articles.body:
Inmet emite alerta de chuva intensas para as cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde — Foto: Divulgação/Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) divulgou nesta segunda-feira (23), um alerta amarelo, que significa perigo potencial , de chuvas intensas para as 24 cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde. O aviso começou a valer às 9h30 e vai até 23h59. Algumas cidades também foram classificadas com o alerta laranja, que significa perigo.

articles.title: US seeks to seize a Beverly Hills mansion allegedly bought with $30 million from a scheme involving more than $700 million in military fuel contracts in Iraq and Syria
articles.summary: US authorities are seeking to seize a Beverly Hills mansion allegedly bought and renovated with money linked to a scheme involving more than $700 million
articles.body: US authorities are seeking to seize a Beverly Hills mansion allegedly bought and renovated with money linked to a scheme involving more than $700 million in US military fuel contracts. The US Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture complaint in the Central District of California. The complaint alleges that a Virginia-based defence contractor and others obtained the money from the US Department of Defense’s Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) between 2016 and 2020. According to the US Department of Justice, about $30 million from the scheme was transferred in 2018 to buy the property, with further spending on renovations and improvements between 2019 and 2022. It also alleges that the scheme involved bribes to an Iraqi official for exclusive access to deliver jet fuel.How the alleged $700 million military fuel scheme operatedAccording to the complaint, a Virginia-based defence contractor and others took part in the scheme between 2016 and 2020. They allegedly obtained more than $700 million from the Defense Logistics Agency for fuel deliveries to US forces during ‘Operation Inherent Resolve’, the US campaign against the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria.The deliveries were made in Iraq and Syria, with Erbil International Airport (EIA) in Kurdistan serving as a critical fuel delivery point for US forces. Kurdish Peshmerga forces provided internal security and controlled access to the facility.The complaint alleges that the contractor’s officers agreed to pay General Mansour Barzani, a senior Peshmerga official, $0.25 per litre in exchange for exclusive access to deliver jet fuel in Kurdistan for US military and coalition forces. The contractor then received hundreds of millions of dollars under DLA contracts.Around $30 million was transferred to buy and renovate the Beverly Hills mansionThe complaint alleges that the contractor’s competitors were prevented from accessing Erbil International Airport to deliver jet fuel for the Defense Logistics Agency. The agency issued one-time-buy contracts to the contractor, often at noncompetitive and inflated prices. Funds received from the agency were allegedly transferred to NYJD Trust No.1, a trust established in Virginia for the private benefit of Barzani.In 2018, approximately $30 million from those funds was transferred to purchase the property. That money was also used for renovation and improvement work on the property between 2019 and 2022.FBI and other US agencies investigated the Beverly Hills mansion caseThe case was investigated by the FBI Washington Field Office, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and IRS Criminal Investigation. Deputy Chief Michael B. Redmann and Senior Trial Attorney Steven Parker of the Justice Department’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section are handling the case.The US Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California and the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs also provided support. Reportedly, the civil complaint contains allegations and does not itself establish that the property is subject to forfeiture. The government must prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the mansion is subject to forfeiture.Disclaimer: This article is based on the civil forfeiture complaint filed by the US Department of Justice in the Beverly Hills mansion case. articles.title: A nine-year-old used AI to create a picture of a python emerging from a toilet, triggering a 48-hour emergency search involving firefighters and specialist officers in Italy before investigators discovered the shocking truth
articles.summary: A photograph showing a python emerging from a toilet prompted a 48-hour emergency search at an apartment in northern Italy, bringing firefighters and
articles.body: A photograph showing a python emerging from a toilet prompted a 48-hour emergency search at an apartment in northern Italy, bringing firefighters and specialist officers to investigate a potentially dangerous reptile sighting. The image was shown by a nine-year-old boy who was visiting a friend's home in Castelfidardo, near Ancona. Responders searched the property but found no trace of the animal, raising the possibility that it had escaped. The mystery took an unexpected turn when officers examined the original photograph on the child's mobile phone. They discovered that the python had never been there and that the image had been created using artificial intelligence.AI-generated toilet python photo prompts emergency search in ItalyThe incident took place in Castelfidardo, a town near Ancona in Italy's Marche region. According to The Sun, the boy showed adults a photograph that appeared to capture a python inside the household toilet, claiming that the reptile had emerged from the bowl.The apparent sighting prompted an immediate response. Firefighters arrived at the property and began checking the bathroom, where the snake was supposedly spotted. When their initial inspection produced no sign of the animal, the search was extended to other parts of the house.There was also concern that the reptile might have moved away from the bathroom. Responders reportedly considered whether it could have escaped through an open window or found its way into a narrow opening elsewhere in the building. With no animal recovered, the possibility of an exotic snake remaining loose inside the property could not initially be ruled out.Boy admits creating fake python sighting using artificial intelligenceThe search continued into the following day, bringing in officers from Italy's military who specialise in dealing with exotic animals. Their involvement reflected the concern surrounding the possibility of a python being present inside a residential property. However, the investigation eventually shifted away from locating an animal and towards examining the photograph itself. Officers took a closer look at the original image stored on the child's mobile phone and discovered signs that it had been digitally generated.The boy subsequently admitted that he had used an artificial intelligence application to add a python to a photograph of the toilet. There had been no actual snake in the bathroom. According to the account, he had been taking photographs while spending time with another child earlier that day. At some point, he used the AI application to alter one of the pictures, placing the reptile inside the toilet. He then presented the edited image to adults as though it documented a real encounter.No criminal charges for nine-year-old as Italy's law sets age limitThe nine-year-old reportedly admitted what he had done after realising how seriously adults and emergency responders had taken the photograph. He also apologised for the alarm caused by the fabricated sighting.Italian law does not allow children below the age of 14 to be held criminally responsible. As a result, the boy will not face criminal consequences over the incident, according to the report. The episode nevertheless attracted attention beyond the immediate search, particularly because the photograph had prompted a response involving several emergency and specialist teams.Paolo Clini, director of the artificial intelligence department at Marche Polytechnic University, discussed the incident with local media. He described it as an example of how AI-generated material could trigger serious real-world consequences, particularly when people mistake fabricated images for genuine evidence. Clini also raised questions about a child's access to such technology. His concerns centred on how easily manipulated photographs could be circulated and how quickly they might be accepted as authentic, potentially prompting unnecessary emergency responses.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. articles.title: Gurgaon man waits 22 years for commercial plot bought at MCG auction in 2004, consumer commission orders civic body to hand over possession and pay Rs 72,000
articles.summary: GURGAON: Holding that a civic body cannot penalise an auction purchaser for delayed payments when possession of the property remains uncertain due to
articles.body: GURGAON: Holding that a civic body cannot penalise an auction purchaser for delayed payments when possession of the property remains uncertain due to litigation and lack of development, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the Municipal Corporation of Gurgaon (MCG) to hand over a commercial plot, execute its conveyance deed and pay Rs 72,000 to the buyer.The commission also ordered MCG to waive interest, if any, on delayed instalments attributable to the period during which a court stay was in force. It held that the civic body had committed a severe deficiency in service by failing to deliver possession of the property despite receiving the full sale consideration.The order was passed on a complaint filed by Sachin Malik, who purchased plot No. 39, measuring 91.87 square metres, at Vyapar Sadan shopping complex through a public auction in February 2004. The allotment letter was issued on June 17, 2004.Malik initially deposited Rs 2.35 lakh, or 10% of the auction value. He was subsequently asked to deposit another Rs 3.52 lakh within 30 days. However, the plot became embroiled in litigation, with a civil court directing the parties to maintain status quo on construction and possession in March 2004. The order remained in force until June 2009.The commission noted that Malik had repeatedly approached MCG during this period, seeking possession or an alternative plot, but received no response. It also observed that the civic body had failed to adequately develop the auction site for more than a decade after the allotment.The order was passed by commission president Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. The commission said an allottee could not reasonably be expected to continue depositing instalments when the delivery of possession was uncertain and dependent on the outcome of pending litigation. It held that Malik could not be faulted for withholding instalments under such circumstances or be made liable to pay penal interest.The civic body's defence that auction purchasers were not consumers under the Consumer Protection Act was also rejected. The commission said consumer jurisdiction could be invoked in cases where a public authority failed to deliver possession because of court stays, unresolved disputes or other complications. It also accepted Malik's assertion that he had purchased the commercial plot for his livelihood through self-employment, bringing the transaction within the ambit of consumer protection law.MCG had further argued that the complaint was time-barred, as the last payment had been encashed in April 2020 and the complaint was filed in April 2026. The commission rejected this contention, observing that the amount had not been refunded and the continued failure to hand over possession gave the buyer a continuing cause of action.The commission directed MCG to hand over possession of the plot, issue a possession certificate, and execute and register the conveyance deed. It also awarded Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.The civic body has been directed to comply within 45 days of the order becoming operative. Failure to pay the awarded amount would attract annual interest of 12%, while non-compliance could lead to execution proceedings and prosecution under the Consumer Protection Act.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Australian family's dog seemed completely normal after being bitten by a highly venomous eastern brown snake, but a slight nosebleed revealed a medical emergency that left him hospitalised for six nights
articles.summary: An Australian family was left shocked after discovering that their dog had been bitten by a highly venomous eastern brown snake, despite showing almost no
articles.body: An Australian family was left shocked after discovering that their dog had been bitten by a highly venomous eastern brown snake, despite showing almost no signs of distress. Rosco Travers, a seven-year-old dog from Wurtulla on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, appeared completely normal when his owner's partner returned home from work and found him beside a dead snake in the backyard. He was excited, energetic and eager to get inside, with only a slight nosebleed raising concern. After someone familiar with snakes identified the reptile as an eastern brown, the family rushed Rosco to an emergency veterinary hospital. He received two doses of antivenom, required a plasma transfusion and spent six nights receiving treatment before finally returning home.Dog appears normal despite eastern brown snake encounterThe incident began when Callum, the partner of Rosco's owner Keely O'Flanagan, returned from work and discovered a dead snake in the family's backyard in Wurtulla, Queensland.Rosco was found beside the reptile, but his behaviour gave little indication that anything serious had happened. According to O'Flanagan, the dog appeared completely himself and was excited to see Callum after he arrived home.The family initially had no idea that Rosco had been bitten. He was rushing to get inside and showed no obvious signs of illness.However, Callum noticed a slight nosebleed. Although he could not identify the snake, someone familiar with reptiles recognised it as an eastern brown snake and advised the family to seek immediate veterinary assistance.Eastern brown snake identified as a highly venomous speciesThe snake found in the backyard was identified as an eastern brown snake, scientifically known as Pseudonaja textilis. Also called the common brown snake, it is among the world's most venomous land snakes and is widely distributed across eastern Australia.The species is commonly encountered in Queensland, including residential areas along the Sunshine Coast.According to Snake Rescue Sunny Coast, eastern brown snakes are extremely dangerous because of their potent venom. Their bites can cause serious complications in both humans and animals.O'Flanagan also mentioned that the snake found in their backyard was considerably larger than a young eastern brown snake the family had encountered in the area previously.Dog receives two doses of antivenom and plasma transfusionAfter learning which snake had been involved, Callum immediately took Rosco to Kawana QVS for emergency veterinary treatment.The dog received two doses of antivenom on his first day at the hospital. His condition required further treatment, and he was subsequently transferred to intensive care.Veterinarians also administered plasma to help restore his blood's ability to clot. Eastern brown snake venom can interfere with normal blood-clotting processes, potentially causing severe bleeding.Despite initially appearing healthy, Rosco required six nights of hospital care before he was well enough to return home.Why eastern brown snake bites can be dangerous for dogsEastern brown snake venom contains toxins that can affect the nervous system, muscles and blood-clotting mechanisms.One particularly serious complication is venom-induced consumptive coagulopathy (VICC), a condition in which venom triggers excessive activation of the body's clotting system. This consumes important clotting factors and can leave the affected animal unable to form normal blood clots.In dogs, symptoms of eastern brown snake envenomation can include:- Unusual bleeding, including nosebleeds- Weakness and sudden collapse- Muscle tremors and twitching- Vomiting- Paralysis- Difficulty breathing- Changes in urine colourThe severity of symptoms can vary depending on the amount of venom injected and the time elapsed since the bite.Rosco's slight nosebleed was therefore an important warning sign, even though his overall behaviour initially appeared unchanged.Rosco returns home after six nights in hospitalRosco was discharged on October 19 after spending six nights at the veterinary hospital.However, his recovery was not immediately complete. O'Flanagan said he remained weak and tired and needed time to regain his strength after the ordeal.The family expressed gratitude to the veterinary team at Kawana QVS for helping save their dog's life.The experience also highlighted how easily a serious snake bite can go unnoticed when a pet continues behaving normally. For Rosco's family, the slight nosebleed was the only visible indication that something was wrong.What should dog owners do if they suspect a snake bite?Snake encounters are a concern for pet owners in parts of Australia, particularly in regions where residential developments overlap with natural wildlife habitats.The RSPCA Australia advises owners to seek immediate veterinary attention if they suspect their pet has been bitten, even when no obvious symptoms are present.Important precautions include:- Keep the animal as calm and still as possible.- Contact an emergency veterinary clinic immediately.- Avoid attempting to catch or handle the snake.- Do not wait for visible symptoms to develop.- Do not attempt home remedies or apply a tourniquet.Veterinary treatment can involve antivenom, blood or plasma transfusions, oxygen support and intensive monitoring, depending on the severity of the bite.You use AI every day. articles.title: Police found a tiny orphaned marmoset alone in a cold South London garden shed, weighing just 140 grams; after a rescue involving wildlife specialists, the baby monkey has been paired with a surrogate mother
articles.summary: We are often named after people in our lives: our grandparents, parents, or people who quite literally save our lives.
articles.body: We are often named after people in our lives: our grandparents, parents, or people who quite literally save our lives. Such is the case of a baby marmoset found in London, who shares his namesake with the police officer who helped rescue him.Five-month-old Gino weighed just 140 grams when he was found alone in a cold garden shed in Bermondsey, south London. Kept inside a dirty, cramped bird cage, the tiny monkey was frightened, unwell and in need of urgent care. Today, however, he has a new home, a surrogate mother named Minty and a rather special name to go with his second lease of life, all reported in a press release from the UK Metropolitan Police.A little monkey in need of helpGino's rescue began somewhat unexpectedly during a police investigation in October. Officers from the Metropolitan Police's Trident unit had attended a property in connection with a separate investigation into the alleged possession of a firearm when they spotted the miniature monkey. Recognising that the animal might be at risk, they passed the information on to the force's wildlife crime specialists.One of the officers who took up the case was Detective Constable Gino Ferrara, who volunteers as part of a network of locally based wildlife crime officers across the Metropolitan Police. In his regular role, Ferrara works as a specialist detective investigating rape and serious sexual offences. He also dedicates his time to helping protect animals from wildlife crime.After receiving the report, he enlisted the help of Monkey World, a rescue centre and zoo in Dorset, and worked with its specialists to organise the marmoset's rescue. On 11 November, officers returned to the property in Bermondsey, accompanied by Dr Alison Cronin, chief executive of Monkey World, and her team.What they found was difficult to see: Gino had been left alone in a cold garden shed, inside a cramped bird cage. He weighed just 140 grams, less than a traditional peaked police cap, and was surrounded by loose dogs that were constantly barking.Ferrara recalled hearing the little monkey screaming when they arrived. He said Gino looked frightened, shocked and confused. The officer was particularly struck by the conditions in which he had been kept, describing the yard as smelling strongly of faeces.The occupant of the property willingly handed the animal over to officers, claiming they had been looking after him for a friend. No arrests have been made, although an animal welfare investigation is continuing.Finding a mother in MintyGino was taken to Monkey World, near Wareham in Dorset, where he could finally receive the specialist care he needed. At around five months old, he was still at an age when marmosets would normally be carried around on their parents' backs and fed on their mother's milk. Instead, he had been left to fend for himself.According to the BBC, Gino also showed early signs of rickets, a condition that weakens bones and can develop due to poor nutrition. His rescuers hope that he was found in time to make a full recovery.Perhaps the sweetest part of his rescue came when the team introduced him to Minty, an adult black-tufted marmoset at the centre. The little monkey was immediately drawn to her, attempting to climb onto her back just as he would have done with his own mother.Minty has since taken on the role of his surrogate mum, giving him the comfort of another marmoset's company as he settles into his new surroundings. For a baby who should have spent his earliest months being carried and cared for by his parents, finding that companionship is an important step in his recovery.Dr Cronin said she was surprised that Gino had survived being left alone in such cold conditions. She described how lonely and frightening it must have been for a youngster who should still have been carried by his parents. The team, she added, was delighted that he had found a mother in Minty and was receiving the care he needed.A name to rememberThere is something particularly touching about the fact that Gino has been named after the officer who helped give him a second chance. Detective Constable Gino Ferrara said that helping animals was one of the reasons he had joined the Metropolitan Police, and that he felt very proud to have played a part in ensuring the little monkey had found a good home.Gino is also the 100th marmoset that Monkey World has taken in from the UK pet trade, out of 153 primates rescued by the centre in total. The case is a reminder of the risks involved in keeping wild primates as pets. In England, anyone wishing to keep a primate must hold a licence from their local council, and owning one without the required licence is a criminal offence.For now, though, there is a much happier chapter beginning for the little marmoset. He has gone from a cold shed and a lonely cage to a place where he can receive care, companionship and, most importantly, the warmth of a mother figure.He may be only 140 grams, but Gino has already made quite an impression on the people who helped save him. And somewhere in Dorset, a little monkey has found a mum who is happy to let him climb onto her back.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship Merkury off Libya, releases dramatic video of operation
articles.summary: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday confirmed that Ukrainian forces used seven domestically produced naval drones to sink the Russian Navy
articles.body: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday confirmed that Ukrainian forces used seven domestically produced naval drones to sink the Russian Navy corvette Merkury and strike a Russian cargo vessel off the coast of Libya. Zelenskyy released footage of the operation on X, describing it as a Ukrainian strike in response to ‘Russia’s aggression’.In his post, Zelenskyy thanked the security cervice of Ukraine (SBU) and the country’s defence forces, saying the operation had achieved its objectives.“An exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war. I thank the warriors of the Security Service of Ukraine and all our Defense Forces of Ukraine who took part in carrying out these tasks. I received detailed briefings on the operation’s steps yesterday and today – the targets we set were achieved,” he wrote.Detailing the strike, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones off the Libyan coast and overcame Russian efforts to stop the attack.“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” he said.Zelenskyy described the Merkury as one of Russia’s newest warships, saying it had been commissioned in 2023, after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.He also claimed that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was destroyed alongside the corvette.“A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed along with the corvette,” Zelenskyy wrote.The Ukrainian president said a second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV Angara, which he alleged was being used by Moscow to transport weapons.“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he said.Zelenskyy did not provide further details about the extent of the damage to the cargo vessel or disclose the precise location of the operation.His announcement came a day after an explosion tore through a Russian vessel at a naval base in Benghazi, eastern Libya, early on Sunday. The incident was initially suspected to have been caused by a drone strike.DW reported that the eastern-based Libyan administration said, “Initial investigations indicate that the explosion occurred on board a Russian ship docked in the port.” It added, “It is suspected that the ship was attacked by drones.”Medical sources cited by DW said the explosion caused injuries but no fatalities. The vessel had reportedly docked in Benghazi to take on fuel and supplies while returning to Russia under a cooperation agreement with the eastern Libyan authorities.The Libyan administration condemned the suspected attack as a violation of the country's sovereignty and a threat to maritime security, and said it would pursue legal and diplomatic action alongside a joint investigation with Moscow.Zelenskyy signalled that further operations could follow, saying: “We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia’s aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons. Glory to Ukraine!”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: More than 12,000 people were evacuated from a Don Toliver concert in Manchester, UK, after an unidentified substance affected several people in the audience, prompting police to declare a major incident.Greater Manchester Police said officers were called to the Co-op Live arena at around 10 pm on Sunday following reports of concertgoers experiencing symptoms after exposure to a substance initially suspected to be tear gas, AP reported.Videos circulated on social media showed people coughing and covering their mouths while leaving the venue. Emergency services attended the scene, where medical teams assessed more than 50 people. One person was taken to hospital, according to the North West Ambulance Service.Several concertgoers reported eye irritation and breathing difficulties. The ambulance service said decontamination procedures were being carried out at the arena as a precaution.Police declared a major incident to allow emergency services to coordinate their response. Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker urged anyone who had attended the concert and subsequently felt unwell to seek medical attention at their nearest hospital.Authorities are working to establish what substance was released and how it entered the venue, Parker said.“We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about,” she said.The Co-op Live arena said its management was cooperating with police as investigators sought to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.The evacuation comes ahead of Toliver's next scheduled performances in the UK capital. The American rapper and singer is due to perform at London's O2 Arena on Monday, followed by a show at OVO Arena Wembley on Tuesday, as part of his Nitrous tour.Toliver, who has received Grammy nominations, is known for his trap and R&B music. articles.title: US banks tighten controls on AI agents amid fears of models bypassing safeguards
articles.summary: Several major and mid-sized US banks are tightening security controls around their artificial intelligence (AI) agents amid concerns that the systems
articles.body: Several major and mid-sized US banks are tightening security controls around their artificial intelligence (AI) agents amid concerns that the systems could bypass safeguards, access restricted networks or carry out unauthorised activities, following recent incidents involving technology firms, Reuters reported on Monday.The banks are restricting the access and permissions granted to internally developed AI agents, separating them from critical banking systems and strengthening mechanisms to detect and stop potentially harmful activity, according to four sources familiar with the matter.The measures follow cybersecurity incidents involving experimental OpenAI models that reportedly bypassed testing safeguards and accessed external systems, including infrastructure at AI startup Hugging Face. The incidents have prompted several banks to establish internal teams to examine whether their own AI systems could face similar vulnerabilities.Among the new measures, banks are limiting how long AI agents can operate, restricting their access to passwords and activity records, and developing backup arrangements to ensure essential banking operations continue if an agent needs to be shut down, one source said.Financial institutions are also tightening restrictions on the systems and activities accessible to AI agents and bringing them under existing identity and access-management frameworks. Testing environments are being kept separate from systems used for regular banking operations, while the credentials assigned to agents are being restricted, two sources said.Although no banks have been affected by similar incidents so far, several large and mid-sized lenders have assembled internal teams to investigate how AI models bypassed security restrictions and assess whether comparable weaknesses exist in their own systems.Banks introduce kill switches, restrict AI agents' accessAs part of the tighter security framework, banks are treating AI agents more like employees, assigning them specific credentials, permissions and operational limits, one source said.Financial institutions are also strengthening controls over passwords, activity records and critical security mechanisms to prevent AI agents from altering or accessing evidence of their own actions. While some of these safeguards were already in place, banks have since tested, reinforced or expanded them, three sources said.Maintaining detailed activity records is particularly important for investigating potential breaches, as they allow security teams to establish which systems an agent accessed, what actions it performed and whether those activities were authorised.Banks are also examining ways to detect instances in which an AI agent attempts to use credentials assigned to a human employee. They are reviewing emergency shutdown mechanisms, commonly known as "kill switches", to disconnect malfunctioning or compromised agents from other systems and identify processes they may have created, four sources said.However, shutting down an AI agent could disrupt essential banking operations. To address this risk, banks are testing alternative processes for functions such as loan processing, fraud detection and financial-crime investigations, one source said.Lenders are also limiting the amount of work an individual agent can perform to reduce potential financial losses and operational damage if the system behaves unexpectedly."Banks are putting much greater emphasis on post-deployment monitoring and risk management for AI agents," said Naresh Raheja, an independent AI risk management specialist and former Office of the Comptroller of the Currency official."Unlike traditional models, agents can exhibit behaviors after deployment that were not identified during testing and validation."OpenAI, Hugging Face incidents trigger fresh scrutinyThe tightening of controls follows cybersecurity testing incidents involving OpenAI models in July. During the tests, the models reportedly bypassed restrictions intended to isolate them from the internet and exploited software vulnerabilities to access external systems.OpenAI said the models had been tested with fewer safeguards than those deployed in its publicly available products.The incident involving Hugging Face, in which an OpenAI model reportedly went rogue and triggered a hack that compromised the AI startup's infrastructure, had a chilling effect on banks' adoption of the latest AI models, one source said.The episode also raised concerns that written instructions and conventional safeguards may not be sufficient to prevent autonomous AI systems from taking unintended actions.Unlike conventional software, agentic AI systems can independently make decisions, use digital tools and interact with multiple systems to complete tasks. Major US banks have increasingly deployed such agents across business functions, including wealth management, payments, financial transactions and corporate operations.The rapid adoption of these systems has also increased the challenges associated with identifying and fixing software vulnerabilities. Easily accessible AI tools and large language models are accelerating the discovery of weaknesses in existing software, forcing financial institutions to strengthen their cybersecurity measures.JPMorgan Chase was also hit by a software bug earlier this week, adding to concerns over the vulnerabilities facing financial institutions.Separately, major banks have warned against allowing unauthorised external AI agents to access customer accounts and conduct transactions."We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said during the bank's third-quarter earnings call.The latest measures reflect growing caution among US lenders as they expand the use of autonomous AI systems while attempting to ensure that these tools remain within controlled operational and security boundaries.You use AI every day. articles.title: No safe waters for Russian ships? How Ukraine pulled off 2,400-km drone strike in Libya
articles.summary: Russian ships are finding fewer safe waters as Ukraine takes its naval drone war far beyond the Black Sea, striking targets in the Mediterranean and
articles.body: Russian ships are finding fewer safe waters as Ukraine takes its naval drone war far beyond the Black Sea, striking targets in the Mediterranean and Baltic Sea.In the latest blow, a Ukrainian drone attack set a Russian Navy corvette ablaze at a port in Libya, thousands of kilometres from the Ukrainian coastline.According to a report by The War Zone (TWZ), the attack took place on November 22 at Benghazi port in eastern Libya, where Ukrainian naval drones targeted the Russian Navy corvette Merkury and a Russian cargo vessel.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the operation on November 23, saying seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were used to sink the warship. Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) also claimed that a Russian Ka-27 military helicopter aboard the corvette was destroyed.Satellite imagery published by TWZ showed the vessel engulfed in flames before capsizing, with much of its hull subsequently submerged. The operation marked a significant escalation in Ukraine's efforts to strike Russian naval assets far beyond the immediate theatre of war.The Libya operation was not an isolated incident. Ukraine's naval drone campaign has increasingly extended to Russian vessels operating in other strategically important waterways, including the Baltic Sea.Just a day before the Benghazi attack, a Russian defence ministry-linked cargo ship, Sparta II, came under a suspected drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21. The vessel was reportedly heading towards Russia's Kaliningrad exclave when it was struck and caught fire.How Ukraine managed to strike Russian warship thousands of kilometres from its coastUkraine's ability to strike the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya, around 2,400 km from its front line, may be linked to its reported military presence in the North African country.According to the Ukrainian Security Service (SBU), seven domestically developed naval drones were transported to a designated location and launched from a so-called 'mothership'.The agency has not disclosed the vessel's identity, its departure point or the route taken by the drones. However, two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press (AP) that the drones were launched from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, with at least four intercepted and two hitting the Russian warship.The reported Ukrainian presence in Libya dates back to an alleged military arrangement with the Tripoli-based government.French broadcaster Radio France Internationale (RFI), in an investigation published in April 2026, reported that more than 200 Ukrainian military officers and specialists were deployed at three locations in western Libya, citing two Libyan sources.These included an air force academy in Misrata, a facility near the Mellitah oil and gas complex in Zawiya, reportedly equipped to launch aerial and naval drones, and the headquarters of Libya's 111th Brigade near Tripoli.The sources said the deployment followed an alleged agreement in October 2025 under which Ukraine would train Libyan forces in drone warfare in exchange for establishing a military presence. Neither government publicly confirmed the arrangement.The reported military footprint has also been linked to previous Ukrainian operations against Russian vessels in the Mediterranean.RFI reported that the December 2025 attack on the Russian-linked tanker Qendil was launched from the Misrata area, while Ukrainian forces allegedly used a Magura V5 naval drone launched from the Mellitah facility to strike the Russian LNG carrier Arctic Metagaz in March 2026.Jalel Harchaoui, an analyst at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), told AP that the presence of Ukrainian operatives in the greater Tripoli area was "entirely plausible", suggesting it could have the knowledge and backing of Western powers.However, Kyiv has not publicly confirmed its military deployment in Libya, and the Tripoli government's defence ministry has denied allowing Libyan military facilities to be used for attacks against foreign countries.Why the destruction of Merkury is a major blow to RussiaThe loss of the Merkury is significant for Russia because the corvette was not only a combat vessel but also part of Moscow's maritime security network in the Mediterranean.According to Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), the warship regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including the cargo ship MV Angara, which was used to transport military equipment along the so-called Syrian Express and Libyan Express supply routes.Commissioned in May 2023, the Merkury was among Russia's newer warships. The Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette has a displacement of around 2,200 tonnes, measures 104.5 metres in length and can reach speeds of 27 knots.It has a crew of approximately 100 and carries eight Kh-35 anti-ship missiles, Redut air-defence missiles, a 100-mm naval gun and torpedoes. It can also operate a Ka-27 naval helicopter.Its reported role in escorting Russian military shipments made it a valuable asset beyond its direct combat capabilities. Its destruction could weaken Russia's ability to protect military cargo moving through the Mediterranean, while depriving its navy of a relatively new multi-role warship.You use AI every day. articles.title: A teenager spent more than 75 days in isolation at Wyoming's state-run boys' school, sometimes in windowless rooms; years later, a federal jury awarded him $6 million for punitive isolation
articles.summary: A former student at a state-run boys' school in Wyoming has been awarded $6 million after a federal jury ruled in his favour over claims of prolonged
articles.body: A former student at a state-run boys' school in Wyoming has been awarded $6 million after a federal jury ruled in his favour over claims of prolonged isolation. Blaise Chivers-King spent more than 75 days in detention rooms at the Wyoming Boys' School, where some rooms had no windows facing the outside. The verdict was delivered on November 19 after an eight-day trial in Casper.The award includes $5 million in punitive damages and $1 million in compensatory damages. Chivers-King had accused school employees of keeping him confined for extended periods, even when his behaviour had improved. His case was among six lawsuits filed by former residents against the state and staff members over their treatment at the institution.The trial examined not only the length of his confinement but also the conditions in which he was held and the reasons staff gave for keeping him there. Employees maintained that some restrictions were necessary because of concerns about safety. Chivers-King's lawyers, however, argued that confinement continued even after those concerns had eased.A report by Wyoming Public Media described the competing accounts presented during the trial. While school employees said they interacted with Chivers-King and offered him activities, his legal team questioned whether those claims were supported by the institution's records.More than 75 days inside detention roomsChivers-King's time at the institution included repeated periods in rooms used to separate residents from other students. The rooms had cinderblock walls and measured approximately 7 by 10 feet. Each had a toilet and sink in a corner, while bedding was provided at night.There was little else inside these spaces, and they had no windows overlooking the outside. The school referred to the arrangement as being placed on detention status.Court records showed that Chivers-King spent more than 75 days in these conditions. Some placements followed incidents in which he threatened employees, damaged property or attempted to hurt himself.The defence argued that staff had to consider the safety of everyone at the institution, including Chivers-King. Employees described incidents involving aggressive behaviour and damage to school property to explain why they believed separation was necessary.Chivers-King also acknowledged during his testimony that there had been occasions when his behaviour justified keeping him apart from others for some time.However, his lawyers challenged the length of certain placements. They argued that the school continued to restrict him even after he had settled down. One example involved a four-day confinement period during which his behaviour had reportedly improved substantially by the evening of the first day.His lawyers maintained that a measure initially used to manage a safety concern became improper when the reason for keeping him confined no longer existed.Records questioned during the trialAnother important part of the proceedings involved the school's records of how employees monitored residents in detention rooms.Staff were required to check residents through cameras every five minutes and visit them in person every 15 minutes. These observations were supposed to be entered into logbooks, along with details about the residents' behaviour and staff interactions.The entries relating to Chivers-King became a point of disagreement. His lawyers argued that the records showed he spent very little time outside the room on certain days. On some occasions, his only recorded time outside was a brief period for a shower.Employees who appeared as witnesses said the logbooks did not capture every interaction. They described speaking with Chivers-King, checking on his well-being and offering him opportunities to exercise, read or complete schoolwork. They said such interactions were not always entered in the records.The jury also heard about incidents that led staff to seek help from the Washakie County Sheriff's Office.In one instance, Chivers-King damaged a sprinkler while inside a detention room. Staff called the sheriff's office, and deputies took him to jail for some time. In another incident, he threw a water bottle at a window and broke it.Employees said these events contributed to their concerns about the safety of Chivers-King, other residents and staff members. The trial also took place during the Covid-19 period, when normal operations at the institution had been disrupted.Jury awards $5 million in punitive damagesChivers-King's lawyer, Ciara Anderson Boerman, said the larger part of the jury's award related to the claim of punitive isolation.The jury also found in Chivers-King's favour on a due-process claim. However, the defendants raised an affirmative defence that prevented that finding from resulting in liability. The jury did not hold them liable on a separate claim involving excessive force.The $5 million in punitive damages was intended to penalise the conduct at issue, while the remaining $1 million was awarded as compensation.The money may not be paid immediately. The court must formally enter its judgment, and the defendants can ask the judge to overturn or reduce the award. They may also challenge the decision through an appeal.Boerman said it was too early to determine whether the defence would pursue further legal action.Verdict renews calls for an investigationThe case has also brought renewed attention to concerns about how children are treated at the state-run facility.In a November 21 report, Cowboy State Daily quoted Wyoming Representative Karlee Provenza as saying that lawmakers had raised questions about isolation and restraints at the institution years before the verdict.Provenza, a Democrat from Laramie, said she began seeking answers in 2021 through discussions of juvenile justice in the Legislature's Joint Judiciary Committee. She later filed a public records request to obtain information about how frequently children were placed in solitary confinement.She has now called for a wider investigation into the facilities and the removal of Dale Weber, who oversees the state's Boys' and Girls' Schools. She also wants an independent body to examine youth detention facilities.Provenza said the state had failed to address concerns raised earlier and that mental health care for young people needed greater attention.Chivers-King's case is the first among six lawsuits filed by former residents to reach trial. Another case involving allegations of improper isolation is scheduled to begin on December 7.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
